wiki_text: In March 2025, Crowley and Naturgy deployed the American Energy, the first U.S.-flagged LNG carrier dedicated to Puerto Rico, in scheduled service between the U.S. Gulf Coast and EcoEletrica's Penuelas facility under a multi-year agreement. The 900-foot, ~130,400 m3 (34.4 million gallon) vessel is operated by Crowley; American Energy transported more than 500 million gallons of LNG to Puerto Rico in its first year of service. Crowley separately operates a co-located LNG loading terminal at Penuelas that draws from the EcoElectrica facility for onward ISO-container/truck distribution to industrial and commercial customers island-wide; this onward domestic distribution is out of scope as its own terminal but is background context on Penuelas's role as a hub.

source_urls.title: Crowley and Naturgy Deploy First U.S. LNG Carrier, American Energy, to Serve Puerto Rico
Crowley launches Puerto Rico LNG hub

wiki_text: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is conducting an ongoing San Juan Harbor dredging and deepening project, widening and deepening the inner-harbor channels serving cruise, petroleum, and LNG terminal operators. Litigation opposing the project (filed by environmental and community groups) explicitly identifies accommodating larger LNG and petroleum tankers as a primary purpose. This is background context on the terminal's operating environment; no specific vessel-size or capacity change is confirmed or implied for the San Juan LNG Terminal itself, and trade-press claims of a specific multiple (e.g. up to 6x current vessel size) were not independently verified -- see the paired qa_review note.
